column2: Ri Bhashabhuti at the tip of the nose; "Ri" Tithisha at the left nostril; "Lri" Sthanu on the right cheek; on the left cheek Hara, "Lri-long";
Katisha in the row of teeth; "Ai" Bhutisha in the upper teeth; "O" Sadyojata on the lower lip; "Au" Anugrahisha on the upper lip;
Am Krura on the throat; "Ah" Mahasena on the tongue; "Ka" Krodhisha on the right shoulder; "Kha" Chandisha on the arms;
Ga Panchantaka on the elbow; "Gha" Shikhi on the right bracelet; "Nga" Ekapada on the fingers; Kurmaka on the left shoulder;
Chha Ekanetra on the arm; "Ja" Chaturvaktra on the elbow; "Jha" Rajasa on the bracelet; "Nya" Sarvakamada on the finger;
Ta Smesha on the hip; "Tha" Langali on the right thigh; "Da" Daruka on the right knee; "Dha" Ardhajaleshvara on the shank;
Na Umakantaka on the fingers; Ashadha on the buttocks; "Tha" Dandi on the left thigh; "Da" Bhida on the left knee;
Dha Mina on the left shank; "Na" Mesha on the toes; "Pa" Lohita in the right belly; "Pha" Shikhi in the left belly;
Ba Galanda on the spine; "Bha" Dvirandaka at the navel; "Ma" Mahakala in the heart; "Ya" Vanisha, not forgotten;
Ra Bhujanga in the blood; "La" Pinaki in the flesh; "Va" Khadgisha in oneself; Vaka in the bone; "Sha" is remembered;
Sha Shveta in the marrow; "Sa" Bhrigu in the seed element; "Ha" Nakulisha in the breath; "Ksha" Samvarta in the treasury;
Having worshipped the Rudra-powers one attains everything with the seed "Hrim."

Thus: "Om, homage to Chamunda Brahmani, Aghora, Amogha, boon-giving, Vichche svaha. Om, homage to Chamunda Maheshvari, Aghora... Om, homage to Chamunda Kaumari... Om, homage to Chamunda Vaishnavi... Om, homage to Chamunda Varahi... Om, homage to Chamunda Indrani... Om, homage to Chamunda Chandi... Om, homage to Chamunda Ishani, Aghora, Amogha, boon-giving, Vichche svaha." The second Vishnu-section of the words by letter: "Om, homage to Chamunda, upward-haired, blazing-crested, lightning-tongued, star-eyed, tawny-browed, of deformed fangs, angry, Om, lover of flesh, blood, liquor and wine, laugh, slayer, slayer, reviver, reviver, Heri Heri Geri Geri Gheri Gheri, Om Muri Muri, Om homage to the host of Mothers, homage, homage, Vichche" — Shambhu's thirty-one words; of the hundred mantras seventy-one.
He Ghaum — beginning and ending with five Oms, one should repeat and worship the three-fold; "He Ghaum" — the heart of Shri Kubjika one should join at the junction of words.
Standing in the three-middle beginning with A-Ku-Ta; in the three-middle of the clans; standing in the three-middle beginning with the middle; the body standing in the three-middle at the foot,

joined with three and a half measures, beginning with Om, the crest-Shiva: "Om Kshraum, homage to Shikhabhairava." "Skhim Skhaum Skhem" — the three-syllable with seed; "Hram Hrim Hraim" — the seedless three-syllable; thirty-two letters supreme;
Ksha and the rest ending in Ka, A-clanless by the order of clans; Shashini, Bhanuni, Pavani, Shiva — thus;
Gandhari, Na, Pindakshi, Chapala, Gajajihvika; Ma, Mrisha, Bhayasara, Madhyama, Pho, Ajara;
Kumari, Kalaratri, Na, Sankata, Da, Dha, Kalika; Pha, Shiva, Bhavaghora, Na, Ta, Bibhatsa, Ta, Vidyuta;
Tha, Vishvambhara, Shamshini, Dha, Jvalamala; Karali, Durjaya, Rangi, Vama, Jyeshtha, and Raudri;
Kha, Kali; Ka, Kulalambi; Anuloma, Da, Pindini; Aa, Vedini; I, Rupi; Shanti, Murti, Kalakula;
Ri, Khadgini; U, Balita; Lri, Kula; Lri-long likewise; Subhaga, Vedanadinya, Karali, Am, and Madhyama;
Ah, Apetaraya — on the seat the powers are to be worshipped in order: "Skham Skhim Skhaum, homage to Mahabhairava." Akshodya, Rikshakarni, Rakshasi, Kshapanakshaya,
Pingakshi, Akshaya, Kshema — the Brahmani eight stand. Ila, Lilavati, Nila, Langa and Lankeshvari,
Lalasa, Vimala, Mala — the Maheshvari eight stand. Hutashana, Vishalakshi, Hrunkari, Vadavamukhi,
Hahārava, Krura, Krodha, Bala, Kharanana — born of Kaumari's body, worshipped, they give all accomplishments.
Sarvajna, Tarala, Tara, Rigveda, Hayanana, Sarasarasvayamgraha, Shashvati — in Vaishnavi's family.
Talujihva, Raktakshi, Vidyujjihva, Karankini, Meghanada, Prachandogra, Kalakarni, Kalipriya —
those born of Varahi's family are to be worshipped by one seeking victory. Champa, Champavati, Prachampa, Jvalitanana,
Pishachi, Pichuvaktra, Lolupa — born of Aindri. Pavani, Yachani, Vamani, Damani,
Bindavela, Brihatkukshi, Vidyuta, Vishvarupini — born of Chamunda's family, worshipped in the mandala for victory.
Yamajihva, Jayanti, Durjaya, Yamantika, Vidali, Revati, Jaya and Vijaya —
born of Mahalakshmi's family; the eight-eights are declared.
Kshem Hrim, to the crest, vaushat; "Kshem, to the armor, hum"; "Hrum, to the three eyes, vaushat"; ending in "Hrim"; and ending in "phat".
Hrimkari, Khechari, Chanda, Chhedani, Kshobhani, Kriya, Kshemakari, Hrimkari, Phatkari — the nine powers.

Now I shall tell the Duris to be worshipped, those in the directions of Indra and the rest: "Hrim Nale Bahutunde Khage Hrim Khechare Jvalani Jvala Kha Khe Chha Chhe Shavavibhishane Chhe Chande Chhedani Karali Kha Khe Chhe Kshe Kharahangi Hrim. Kshe Vakshe Kapile Ha Kshe Hrum Krun Tejovati Raudri Mata Hrim Phe Ve Phe Phe Vakre Vari Phe. Puti Puti Ghore Hrum phat Brahmavetali" — in the middle the secret limbs and principles of Tvarita I tell again:
Hraum Hrum Hah is said for the heart; "Hom Hah" for the head; "Pham Jvala Jvala" the crest; armor "Ile Hram Hum Hum";

Krom Kshum Shrim is called the eye; "Kshaum" the weapon, then "phat"; "Hum Khe Vachchhe Kshe Hrim Kshem Hum phat" or "Hum" the head in the middle; in the east and others Khe Sadashive; Va Isha; Chhe Manonmani; Maksha Tarkshya; Hrim Madhava;
Kshem Brahma, "Hum" Aditya, "Darunam phat" are always remembered.
The pericarp and filaments; the orb of sun, moon and fire; Dipta, Sukshma, Jaya, Bhadra, Vibhuti, Vimala,
Amogha, Vidyuta to be worshipped; the ninth Sarvatomukhi. Sattva, rajas and tamas, nature and the Person;
one should worship the Self, the inner Self and the Supreme Self; all joined with bindu and with wind of illusion;
Usha, Prabha and Sandhya, Saya, Maya joined with strength; joined with bindu and Vishnu, the eight door-guards likewise;
one should worship Surya, Chanda and Prachanda with scent and the rest; by worship, repetition, oblation and the rest, victory comes in battle and the like.
Having repeated the Gayatri in the water one should do it sixteenfold; and breath-controls in the forenoon, one should offer the oblation in the fire;
living on alms, barley gruel, or eating fruits and roots, living on milk, barley meal and ghee, one should rely on a single meal;
until the hundred-thousand oblation is completed, Parvati. The fee at the end of the hundred-thousand oblation: cows, garments and gold.
On the rise of all portents, with five or ten Brahmins: there is no portent in the world that is not calmed by this.
There is no auspiciousness higher than that which exceeds this. The king who has a crore oblation done by Brahmins as before,
his enemies never stand in battle at any time; no epidemic or disease arises anywhere in his country.
Excess rain, lack of rain, rats, locusts, parrots, Rakshasas and the rest are calmed, and all enemies in battle.
In the crore oblation one should choose twenty Brahmins, or a hundred or a thousand; one obtains prosperity as desired.
A Brahmin, king or merchant who performs the crore oblation obtains whatever he desires and goes bodily to heaven.
With the Gayatri or planet-mantras, or Kushmandi and Jatavedas, with Indra, Varuna, Vayu, Yama, Agni and Vishnu mantras,
with Shakta, Shambhava and Saura mantras, by oblation and worship thereafter; with ten thousand a small accomplishment; a hundred-thousand oblation removes all affliction;
for the destruction of all troubles the crore oblation gives all aims. Barley, rice, sesame, milk, ghee, kusha, pramatika,
lotus, vetiver, bilva and mango leaves are declared for the oblation. The pit for crore oblations is of eight cubits,
half of that is prescribed for a hundred-thousand oblation. Oblation with ten thousand and a hundred thousand and a crore with ghee and the rest is declared.
Sons led by Ikshvaku; Hari was by part. In Svayambhuva's, Manasa; after that Ajita;
Satya, Hari, Devadara, Vaikuntha, Vamana in order; the eighth Manu, born of Chhaya, will be the son of the Sun;
he is like the earlier one, Savarni, the eighth; the Sutapa and other host of gods, Diptimat, Dronika and others as sages,
Bali is Indra, Viraja and others the sons. The ninth, Daksha-Savarni; the Paras and others are then the gods;
Indra is Adbhuta among them; Savana and others best of Brahmins; Dhritaketu and others the sons; thus Brahma-Savarni;
Sukha and others the host of gods; their Shanti, Shatakratu; Havishya and others the sages; Sukshetra and others their sons;
then Dharma-Savarni; then Vihangama and others the gods; Ganesha is Indra, Nashchara and others the sages desiring sons;
Sarvatraga and others called Rudra; the Savarni will be the Manu; Ritadhama the king of gods, Harita and others the deities,
Tapasya and others the seven sages; sons with Vaidevavat at the head; the thirteenth Manu Raucya; Sutramana and others the gods;
Indra Divaspati, crusher of demons and the rest; Nirmoha and others the seven sages; Chitrasena and others sons;
the fourteenth Manu Bhautya; Shuchi will be Indra; the Chakshusha and others the host of gods; Agnibahu and others the twice-born;
the sons of the fourteenth Manu Bhautya: Urumukha and others. The seven sages of heaven drive the gods on earth;
the gods are sacrifice-enjoyers; the earth is protected by sons. In Brahma's day, O Brahmin, there are fourteen Manus.
Hari divided the Veda at the end of Dvapara, from Manu and the rest. The first Veda was four-footed, measured by a hundred thousand;
the Yajurveda was one; he divided it fourfold; the sage made the Adhvaryu office with Yajus verses and the Hotri with Rik verses;
the Udgatri with Samans, and the Brahma priesthood with the Atharvans. First Pailu, Vyasa's disciple, master of the Rigveda;
Indra gave the collection to Pramati and to Vaskala; he gave to Baudhya and others, and he made his own collection fourfold.
The twenty-seven branches of the Yajurveda tree the wise Vaishampayana, Vyasa's disciple, made.
The Kanva, Vajasaneya and others are remembered with Yajnavalkya and others. The branches of the Samaveda tree: Vyasa's disciple Jaimini,
Sumantu and Sukarma — each took a collection; the teacher called Sukarma took a thousand collections;
and Sumantu, Vyasa's disciple, divided the Atharva tree; he taught thousands of disciples, the Paippaladas.
By Vyasa's grace the Suta made the Purana-collection.
Pukkasa is the son of a Kshatriya woman by a Shudra, born in reverse order; Magadha likewise from a Vaishya; Ayogava from a Shudra.
In a Vaishya woman from reverse-order men are thousands of reverse-order castes. Marriage among them is with equals, not with higher nor lower.
The work of the Chandala is declared as the killing of those to be executed; the livelihood of Vaidehaka by women's protection;
of Sutas, horse-driving; of Pukkasas, hunting; the work of praise for Magadhas, and likewise for Ayogava;
entering the stage is declared, and livelihood by crafts, residence outside the village, wearing the clothes of the dead;
contact with a Chandala is not allowed by others. Whoever here gives up the body for a Brahmin or for a cow,
or for women and children and the like, it is the cause of success for outcastes. In mixed cases castes are to be known from the work of father and mother.
A name ending in Gupta and Dasa is praised for Vaishyas and Shudras; one ending in Sharma is told for a Brahmin and in Varma for a Kshatriya;
a name with Gupta and Dasa is praised for Vaishyas and Shudras. One should present the child to the husband: "This is your son."
The tonsure according to family; the initiation of a Brahmin in the eighth year from conception, or the eighth; for a king in the eleventh from conception.
